name: Aether Blood
descriptionMarkdown:
*Adventuring Gear, rare*

---

The most extravagant rumors claim the creation of this glowing purple liquid requires the blood of a unicorn -- a creature generally regarded as mythical. Regardless of the truth, the potent magic in a vial of Aether Blood leads many spellcasters to carry it for use in dire circumstances.

Consuming this potion enhances your spellcasting prowess for 1 minute. While the effect lasts, add 1 to the saving throw DCs for the spells you cast. In addition, whenever your spell could be cast using a higher-level spell slot, increase the spell's effective level by 1.

Prolonged use of Aether Blood is grueling. You can consume it safely a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum 1). Any further use results in painful addiction. While addicted, you have Disadvantage|XPHB on Strength and Constitution ability checks and saving throws, and attack rolls against you have Advantage|XPHB.

Consuming another vial of Aether Blood negates this effect until you finish a Long Rest|XPHB, but you must also make a DC 10 Charisma save. On a failure, you become lethargic, and your Speed|XPHB is reduced by 20 feet for 1 minute.

The addiction lasts until you receive a Greater Restoration spell, or until you have not consumed Aether Blood for 30 days.

name: Arc Rifle
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, very rare*

---

In the unforgiving lands of Etharis, having reliable and efficient weapons is as essential as carrying water and food.

In that regard, skilled inventors are highly sought, and among them gnomes are the most renowned. However, innovation can sometimes go too far, and the Arc Rifle is the perfect example of how.

This part-science, part-arcane contraption is a rifle-like weapon housing glass tubes of sparking electricity and powered by a small perpetual motion device. Invented by a team of famous gnome engineers, it literally shoots lightning, hitting the target faster than other missile weapons and reducing flesh to ashes in mere seconds. Due in part to this tremendous efficiency, this weapon was quickly declared illegal in most regions of Etharis. It is also believed to destroy the target's soul when it kills them.

The rifle has 4 charges. You can expend 1 charge as a Magic action to launch a torrent of lightning in a 60-foot long, 5-foot-wide Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line. Each creature in the Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line must make a 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 4d6 Lightning damage, or half as much on a successful save.

**Regaining Charges.** The rifle regains 1d4 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll

1d20. On a 1, the rifle becomes a useless hunk of metal and glass.

name: Ardor
descriptionMarkdown:
*Martial Weapon, artifact (Requires Attunement)*

**Damage:** 1d8 slashing (or 1d10 slashing versatile) | **Properties:** Versatile | **Weight:** 4 lb

---

The blades of this axe smolder with an inner light, and the dark wooden handle is accented with silver. After the celestial realm turned back yet another assault from the forces of evil, a fiendish forge master received a vision, allowing them to craft a weapon like no other. Ardor now lies in a hidden vault, waiting to be wielded by a scion of darkness who strikes on behalf of the forces of the Arch Daemons.

The fiends don't realize that an equally powerful weapon rests in the hands of the celestials, who wage eternal war against them. In the interest of maintaining order, the fates who inspired the forgemaster to craft Ardor also sent a similar vision to a smith of heaven.

**Axe of Hell.** This magic battleaxe grants a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it. When you hit with it, the target takes an extra 2d10 Necrotic damage.

**Champion of Evil.** While holding the battleaxe, you have Immunity|XPHB to the Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, and Stunned conditions.

**Ardor's Pursuit. Ardor's Pursuit:.** You can take a Bonus Action|XPHB to toss the axe into the air, causing it to hover magically in your space. While the weapon hovers, you can take a Bonus Action|XPHB to cause it to fly up to 50 feet to another spot within 50 feet of you. As part of the same Bonus Action|XPHB, you can either grasp the weapon if it is within reach, or cause it to attack one creature within 5 feet of the weapon. The weapon uses your attack roll and adds your ability modifier to the damage rolls. The weapon ceases to hover if you grasp it, if you are more than 50 feet away from it, or if you die.

**Spells.** While the axe is on your person, you can use a Magic action to cast one of the following spells (save DC 18): Bane, Bestow Curse, or Incendiary Cloud. Once you use the axe to cast a spell, that spell can't be cast again from it until the next dawn.

**Destroying the Axe.** The only thing capable of damaging the battleaxe is its celestial twin, Zeal. A creature wielding Zeal can choose to attack Ardor, which has an Armor Class|XPHB of 21 and 300 HP. No other creature or object can damage Ardor.

name: Banshee Box
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, common*

---

This ivory music box is inlaid with silver decorations depicting tiny scenes of gruesome violence. If a creature holds the box for at least one minute, they can use a Magic action to mentally command the box to make a sound or phrase of their choosing, lasting up to one minute. Once the lid is open, that sound or phrase continues to play on a loop until the box is closed. If the person who created the repeating sound travels more than 300 feet away from the box, the lid closes and the music box ceases to play.

The box can create any soundscape, like haunting piano music, the sounds of a lively party, a spoken phrase, or a continuous series of screams. When the Magic action is used to create the sounds, the user can also choose whether the sound is audible in an Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation with a 5-foot radius, a 30-foot radius, or a 120-foot radius.

**Damage:** 1d8 piercing | **Properties:** Ammunition, Heavy, Two-Handed | **Weight:** 2 lb

---

This white wooden bow is set with four gemstones: a ruby, an emerald, a sapphire, and a diamond.

When you hold this bow, as a Bonus Action|XPHB you can summon a magical arrow composed of one of the four elements. You must still make an attack roll to hit a creature with the magical arrow, and it does only the damage listed.

When you take the Attack action, you can attack with this summoned arrow. If you have a feature that lets you fire more than one arrow on a turn, you can fire other arrows as part of the Attack action.

Each time you summon a magical arrow, you must choose one of the four options below. If you do not fire the arrow within 1 minute of summoning it, it dissolves.

- **Arrow of Air.** On a hit, the arrow of air deals 4d8 Lightning damage.
- **Arrow of Earth.** On a hit, the arrow of earth deals 4d8 Bludgeoning damage.
- **Arrow of Fire.** On a hit, the arrow of fire deals 4d8 Fire damage.
- **Arrow of Water.** On a hit, the arrow of water deals 4d8 Cold damage.

**Boon of Empyreus.** For one minute, you gain a +2 bonus to Armor Class|XPHB, and you add 1d4 to the first attack roll you make each of your turns. If you would receive this boon again before the next dawn, you instead take 3d6 Radiant damage and the boon is not applied.

**Boon of Beleth.** For one minute, an aura radiates from you in a 10-foot radius. When an enemy ends its turn in the area, it must succeed on a 14 Wisdom saving throw or have the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn. While the aura lasts, you deal an extra 1d6 Psychic damage whenever you hit a Frightened creature with a weapon attack. If you would receive this boon again before the next dawn, you instead take 3d6 Necrotic damage and the boon is not applied.

descriptionMarkdown:

---

Some people have no qualms about exploiting any opportunity for profit, including the sorrow caused by the loss of a loved one. Such people would appreciate the Collar of the Undead, whether as con artists looking for bereaved individuals to fleece, or as dark sorcerers in need of souls.

As an action, you can place this collar around the neck of a Humanoid creature of Large size or smaller that has died within the last 10 days. The creature returns to life with 1 Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point. The creature uses its normal game statistics, except that its creature type becomes Undead and it doesn't need to eat, sleep, or breathe. If its Hit Points|XPHB are reduced to 0, the creature is utterly destroyed, turning into dust.

Each dawn, the creature's Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point Maximum decreases by 1d4 as its soul slowly slips away. When the creature's Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point Maximum reaches 0, or its Hit Points|XPHB are reduced to 0, it falls apart into a heap of dust and is destroyed.

If you issue no commands, the creature takes the Dodge action and moves only to avoid harm. Once given an order, the creature continues to follow it until its task is complete.

If the collar is removed, the creature is immediately reduced to 0 Hit Points|XPHB.

descriptionMarkdown:
*Adventuring Gear, uncommon*

---

Made from a mysterious, magically grown plant, this popular new drug induces vivid hallucinations in which the user's dreams appear to be fulfilled. Some users even see visions of branching possibilities that their life could take.

Upon consuming Dreams Leaves, you can choose to fall into a blissful, trance-like state for 1 hour, during which time you have the Unconscious condition. Taking damage ends the trance early.

If you remain in the trance for the full hour, you awaken with a faint insight into your future. Once before you finish your next Long Rest|XPHB, you can take a Reaction|XPHB to reroll a D20 Test|XPHB and use the new result.

Using this Reaction|XPHB creates an addiction to Dreams Leaves. While addicted, you have Disadvantage|XPHB on saving throws. Consuming another dose of Dreams Leaves negates this effect until you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

The addiction lasts until you receive a Greater Restoration spell, or until you have not consumed Dreams Leaves for 30 days.

name: Full Moon Extract
descriptionMarkdown:
*Adventuring Gear, uncommon*

---

This potent powder is supposedly created by grinding up the dried organs of a werewolf. Despite the risks associated with its use, it is a favored drug of many wrestlers, boxers, and soldiers because of the raw strength it provides.

Consuming this potion enhances your physical prowess for 1 hour. While the effect lasts, your Strength score becomes 19 (unless it was already 19 or higher), and you have Advantage|XPHB on Strength ability checks and saving throws.

Prolonged use of Full Moon Extract is risky. You can consume it safely a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum 1). Any further use results in painful addiction. While addicted, you have Disadvantage|XPHB on Dexterity ability checks and saving throws, and attack rolls against you have Advantage|XPHB.

Consuming another dose of Full Moon Extract negates this effect until you finish a Long Rest|XPHB, but you must also make a 10 Charisma save. On a failure, you become overcome by violent urges for 1 minute. During that time, you cannot take Bonus Action|XPHB|Bonus Actions or reaction|XPHB|Reactions. At the start of each of your turns, you regard the creature nearest to you that you can see or hear as your enemy. During that turn, you must move as close to the creature as possible and take the Attack action, targeting the creature. If your movement doesn't bring you within reach, you must use your Dash action to continue moving toward it.

The addiction lasts until you receive a Greater Restoration spell, or until you have not consumed Full Moon Extract for 30 days.

descriptionMarkdown:

---

This bubbling liquid is distilled from the remains of a magebane ooze. You can throw the container at an enemy's weapon or armor, or at a spellcaster.

name: Magical Prosthetics
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, varies*

---

The brutal warfare and vicious monsters prevalent across Etharis leave many with Grievous Wounds|GrimHollowCG24, including missing limbs and other potentially debilitating injuries. The engineers and crafters of the world have made great strides in helping those people deal with those injuries through Prosthetics, which are covered in Chapter 5 of the Grim Hollow Player's Guide|GrimHollowPG24|5.

Magical versions of Prosthetics can be crafted with properties that mimic existing Wondrous Items or Rings. Typically, these Prosthetics replicate the body part that would wear that item. For example, a Magical Prosthetic leg could replicate the effect of Boots of Elvenkind, while a Magical Prosthetic hand might act as a Ring of Protection.

A Magical Prosthetic has the same rarity as the magic item it mimics. It counts as "wearing" an item of that kind, so if you have a Magical Prosthetic leg that mimics Boots of Elvenkind, you can't wear another pair of magic boots.

descriptionMarkdown:
*Simple Weapon, very rare (by a Fighter or Barbarian)*

**Damage:** 1d8 bludgeoning | **Properties:** Two-Handed | **Weight:** 10 lb

---

This weapon is a blunt but jagged-edged bludgeon that is the object form of a kokela. You gain a +4 bonus to damage rolls made with this weapon, and attack rolls made with this weapon score a Critical Hit|XPHB on a roll of 19 or 20. If you have abilities that increase your critical range with melee attack rolls, this weapon scores a Critical Hit|XPHB on a roll of 17-20.

**Curse.** This weapon is cursed. Attuning to it curses you until you spend one year at least a mile away from the weapon. While you remain cursed, you're unwilling to part with the club, always keeping it within reach. You also have Disadvantage|XPHB on attack rolls with weapons other than this one, unless no foe is within 60 feet of you that you can see or hear.

Whenever you roll a Critical Hit|XPHB with this weapon, after dealing damage there is a 25% chance the Malleus Macabre casts Cloudkill at level 9 centered on you.

descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, very rare (Requires Attunement)*

---

Created through a gruesome process requiring the muscle tissue of a bugbear vampire, this graft melds to the flesh of a living creature who attunes to it. Your Strength increases by 2, to a maximum of 30. When you become attuned, you must succeed on a 15 Constitution save or your Constitution decreases by 2, to a minimum of 1.

**Curse.** This graft is cursed. Attuning to it curses you for 1 year or until you are targeted by Remove Curse or a similar spell. Removing the graft fails to end the curse on you, and you cannot end the Attunement|XPHB while the curse lasts. You develop a deep desire for rare meat and raw blood. At the end of each week, you must succeed on a 10 Constitution saving throw or become a Vampire Spawn with no progenitor.

name: Soulbond Stone
descriptionMarkdown:

This smooth and weighty stone has a dusk-colored gem embedded in its center. When pressed to the chest of a creature who has been dead for less than one minute, the stone captures a fragment of the dead creature's soul for later use.

name: Staff of the Sorcerer King
descriptionMarkdown:
*Adventuring Gear, legendary (Requires Attunement)*

---

This ebony staff bears a bronze spear tip and additional blades carved to depict a winged scarab. The staff can be wielded as a magic spear that grants a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it. You are considered proficient with this weapon while you are attuned to it, even if you aren't proficient with spears. While holding the staff, you gain these benefits:

- **Spell Power.** You gain a +2 bonus to spell attack rolls.
- **Cull Subjects.** Humanoids have a -2 penalty to saving throws against your spells.
- **Spell Shield.** You have Advantage|XPHB on saving throws against spells that target only you.

**Cursed.** This staff is cursed, and becoming attuned to it extends the curse to you. Until the curse is broken with Remove Curse or similar magic, you are unwilling to part with the staff, keeping it within reach at all times. In addition, you have Disadvantage|XPHB on attack rolls made with weapons other than this one.

While cursed, you must make a 17 Constitution saving throw each day at midnight. On a failed save, your Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point maximum is reduced by 10 unless you are Undead. Your Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point maximum can only be restored by a Wish spell. If your Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point maximum is reduced to 0 while cursed, you die and immediately rise as a Wight.

descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, rare*

---

This magical spying device, designed by gnome engineers on behalf of the Ebon Syndicate, is composed of two crystal orbs. The Emitter Orb is marble-sized, making it easy to slip into your target's purse or pocket. The Receiver Orb is fist-sized.

You can take a Magic action and touch the two orbs together to activate them for 7 days. Once activated, the Emitter Orb begins capturing thoughts within a 5-foot Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere centered on it. On a failed save, the holder of the Received Orb becomes immediately aware of that creature's surface thoughts for 1 minute, even if it leaves the area.

descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, very rare*

---

This ornate hand mirror, made of carved iron and adorned with images of grasping hands, can be used to contact other planes. As a Magic action, you can speak the true name of an extraplanar being, such as a Fey, Fiend, or Celestial, into the mirror three times. This summons the named creature in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the mirror.

A creature summoned this way retains its free will, and there is no guarantee it views you as an ally. It cannot leave this plane for 1 minute, after which time it automatically returns to its home plane unless it has the means to travel between planes on its own, in which case it can choose to stay.

name: Ulmyr's Eye (Adept)
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, artifact (Requires Attunement)*

---

Ulmyr's Eye appears to be a crystal ball filled with ever-shifting smoke. Peering into the orb reveals hazy visions, many of which are disturbing.

**Aspirant.** At this tier of Attunement|XPHB, you have the following benefits:

- You know the Guidance cantrip and can cast it even if you don't have the Spellcasting class feature.
- The orb has 12 charges. You can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells (save 18) from it: Augury (2 charges), Clairvoyance (3 charges), Detect Thoughts (2 charges), Divination (4 charges), or Scrying (5 charges). The orb regains 2d4 + 4 expended charges at dawn.

You also gain the following curse:

- Your fears of the future diminish your attention in the present. While attuned to Ulmyr's Eye, you have Disadvantage|XPHB on Wisdom (Perception) and Intelligence (Investigation) checks.

**Adept.** At the Adept tier of Attunement|XPHB, you have the following additional benefits:

- While holding the orb, you can use your Reaction|XPHB to give Advantage|XPHB or Disadvantage|XPHB on a roll when a creature you can see within 60 feet makes D20 Test|XPHB. The triggering creature rerolls and uses the new result. You can use this property a number of times equal to your Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.
- While holding the orb, you can expend 1 or more of its charges to cast one of your prepared spells without expending a spell slot. The number of charges expended is equal to the spell's level.

You also gain the following curse:

- Ulmyr's Eye fills your dreams and meditations with nightmarish visions, making it difficult for you to rest. When you finish a Long Rest|XPHB, you must succeed a 14 Wisdom saving throw or gain only the benefits of a Short Rest|XPHB instead.

name: Zeal
descriptionMarkdown:
*Adventuring Gear, artifact (Requires Attunement)*

---

This warhammer glows with an inner light. When the celestial realm nearly fell, a heavenly smith received a vision, to craft a hammer like no other. With the might of Zeal, heaven's armies turned back their foes, restoring the cosmic balance.

Zeal lies lost somewhere in Etharis, waiting to be wielded against the forces of darkness. The celestials don't realize that the forces of darkness hold an equally powerful weapon, as the fates that inspired Zeal's creation sent a similar vision to an infernal weaponsmith to maintain the balance of power.

**Hammer of Heaven.** This magic warhammer grants a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it. When you hit with it, the target takes an extra 2d10 Radiant damage.

**Champion of Good.** While holding Zeal, you have Immunity|XPHB to the Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, and Stunned conditions.

**Zealous Pursuit.** You can take a Bonus Action|XPHB to toss the hammer into the air, causing it to hover magically in your space. While the weapon hovers, you can take a Bonus Action|XPHB to cause it to fly up to 50 feet to another spot within 50 feet of you. As part of the same Bonus Action|XPHB, you can either grasp the weapon if it is within reach, or cause it to attack one creature within 5 feet of the weapon. The weapon uses your attack roll and adds your ability modifier to the damage rolls. The weapon ceases to hover if you grasp it, if you are more than 50 feet away from it, or if you die.

**Spells.** While the hammer is on your person, you can cast Beacon of Hope, Earthquake, or Heroism (save 18) from the weapon. Once you use Zeal to cast a spell, that spell can't be cast again from it until the next dawn.

**Destroying the Hammer.** The only thing capable of damaging Zeal is its fiendish twin Ardor. A creature wielding Ardor can choose to attack Zeal, which has an Armor Class|XPHB of 21 and 300 Hit Points|XPHB. No other creature or object can damage Zeal.
